ashley (Docs): Heads up — we're publishing the Python SDK v2.0.0-rc1 to PyPI and pushing a docs refresh. This release is async-first and deprecates the legacy sync client. Please skim the migration notes and flag any missing examples. RC -> 2 weeks -> GA schedule. :tada:

samir (SDK): Changelog summary: async-first Client API, generate() renamed to text_generate(), streaming via async iterators, default model selection changed for latency optimizations. Breaking: sync.Client is deprecated and scheduled for removal in v3.0 (approx 6 months).

samir (SDK): Migration example (old -> new):
```python
# old sync usage
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="${API_KEY}")
resp = c.generate('Write a haiku')
print(resp.text)

# new async usage
from redwood.async_sdk import AsyncClient
c = AsyncClient(api_key="${API_KEY}")
resp = await c.text_generate('Write a haiku')
async for chunk in resp.stream():
    print(chunk.text)
```

samir (SDK): We'll publish a shim package (redwood-compat) to ease transition for a short window, but we strongly recommend migrating to async to get batching + KV caching benefits.

docs-bot: Published docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/sdk/python/async-migration — contains API diffs, full examples, and a FAQ. :link:

maria (Eng): Quick question — do we expect any perf regressions for low-concurrency clients?

samir (SDK): Good Q. In our benchmarks async yields ~15% p95 latency improvements under realistic traffic due to continuous batching. For extremely low concurrency single-request clients, behavior should be similar; default model switch might change median slightly if users relied on implicit model selection. We'll note that in the FAQ.

kevin (DevEx): Docs action items: add a migration banner on sync pages, fold the new async quickstart into examples repo, and schedule a 30-min migration webinar next Wed. I'll set up the calendar and draft slides.

ashley (Docs): Thanks — I'll add a deprecation timeline section in the top-level SDK page and link to the shim. We'll also add a short note in the changelog about the deprecation date and the compatibility window. :white_check_mark:
